clue.text: Lectures on ethnicity in Aintree, for example?

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it, so the lectures part comes second

parts.note: a race is a group sharing ethnicity
a course is a series of lectures

explanation.surface: Someone giving talks about ethnic background at the Grand National venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National steeplechase; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a well-known venue where horses compete, an example of such a track.

clue.text: Stupid Greek character hiding in tree

indicators.note: the Greek letter is concealed within the tree's name, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the ash is a common tree
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A dim Greek person lurking up a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Ape-like behaviour suggests silliness or foolishness, so the word can mean daft.

clue.text: Morally correct, as the laic could become

indicators.note: the words the laic could be turned into something else, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lay person might turn into a virtuous one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could become' shuffles THE LAIC; 'laic' means lay, not clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Principled conduct that follows moral standards is described with this word.

clue.text: Other ranks carrying a blade for use in a row?

definitions.text: blade for use in a row?

indicators.note: the abbreviation holds the letter A within it, as a soldier carries a load

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Ordinary soldiers bearing a sword to use in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a row' looks like a quarrel and 'blade' a sword; here rowing a boat is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower uses a long pole with a flat blade to propel a boat.

clue.text: Search in grass as asked

indicators.note: the search word is placed inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wetlands
a quest is a search

explanation.surface: Someone combing the long grass because they were told to.
explanation.definitionFit: Something asked for has been solicited or sought from someone.

clue.text: One of the Sitwells noted it here in the centre

indicators.note: the letters sit in the middle of the words noted it here, concealed within them

explanation.surface: A literary family member noted something down at this very spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sitwells were a 20th-century English literary family: Edith, Osbert and Sacheverell.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet among the three Sitwell siblings was Dame Edith, the eldest sister.

clue.text: Second husband knowledgeable about Japanese religion

parts.note: being into a subject means being keen on and knowledgeable about it

explanation.surface: A woman's second husband is an expert on Japanese faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the traditional native faith of Japan, honouring kami spirits.

clue.text: Spot a woman's plucked instrument

parts.note: a zit is a pimple or spot
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: Catch sight of the stringed instrument belonging to some woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a verb meaning see; it is a pimple.
explanation.definitionFit: This flat stringed instrument is played by plucking its many strings.

clue.text: Parisian who introduces revolutionary savoury tart

indicators.note: the first piece leads in and introduces the second, so it comes before it

parts.note: qui is French for who, as a Parisian would say it
Che Guevara is the stock crossword revolutionary

explanation.surface: A Frenchman presents a radical with a flan.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiche is an open pastry case filled with egg custard, a classic savoury flan.

clue.text: Fashionable greeting in Conservative circles primarily

indicators.note: the greeting goes inside the two letters formed by the abbreviation and the initial
primarily points to the first letter of circles

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: A trendy hello heard among Tory social sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chic is stylish and elegant, in vogue.

clue.text: Observe article, displaying extreme anger

parts.note: to see is to observe
an article is an item, a thing

explanation.surface: Watching an item that shows someone's fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' tempts toward A, AN or THE, but here it means an object.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone furious but containing it is said to be boiling over inwardly, fuming.

clue.text: Quite a paper — now and then!

parts.note: some can mean quite a, as in 'that was some party'
The Times is a newspaper

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising a newspaper's quality, read occasionally.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark nods to the setter's own paper, The Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something occasionally, not always, is doing it at intervals.

clue.text: Sanctuary unknown in a squalid area

indicators.note: the unknown letter goes inside the combined pieces

parts.note: a slum is a squalid run-down area
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A refuge for strangers found in a run-down district.
explanation.definitionFit: Political refuge granted to someone fleeing persecution is a form of sanctuary.

clue.text: Salutation upset mother, sad to say

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the pieces upside down, reading them from bottom to top

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
alas means sadly, sad to say

explanation.surface: Greeting someone's mother who regrettably got upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an anagram signal; in a down answer it turns MA ALAS over.
explanation.definitionFit: A low bow with the hand to the forehead, used as a greeting in Muslim countries.

clue.text: Extremely tricky scam involving old business magnate

indicators.note: extremely points to the outermost letters of tricky
the scam word wraps around the old letter

parts.note: a con is a scam

explanation.surface: A very devious fraud by a former business mogul.
explanation.definitionFit: A tycoon is a wealthy, powerful industrialist.

clue.text: Box containing Low's second satirical drawing

indicators.note: the box holds that letter inside it

parts.note: a carton is a box

indicators.note: second points to the second letter of Low's

explanation.surface: A box holding another satirical sketch by the cartoonist Low.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir David Low was a famous political cartoonist, so the surface fits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon is a humorous drawing, often mocking politicians.

clue.text: Shut away nearby with 1950s youth

parts.note: close means nearby
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress

explanation.surface: A Teddy boy locked up close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shut in a room for privacy or secrecy is kept private, out of sight.

clue.text: Do away with rough vegetation

definitions.meaning: to cancel or abandon a plan

explanation.surface: Clear out the wild undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means cancel a plan; the noun is stunted bushland.

clue.text: Work in outskirts of Rochdale making stout cord

indicators.note: the work goes inside the edge letters
outskirts points to the first and last letters of Rochdale

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Labour on the edge of a Lancashire town producing strong cord.
explanation.walkthrough: Rochdale is a town in Greater Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Rope is thick strong cord made from twisted strands.

clue.text: Urge to identify a section of the media

definitions.meaning: to push someone hard to do something

explanation.surface: An encouragement to name a part of the media.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to insist; the noun is newspapers and journalists as a body.

clue.text: Grass in which a couple of sheep are head to head

indicators.note: two animals face each other only if the first one is turned round to meet the second

parts.note: a couple of sheep means two male sheep; this phrase supplies the first ram
a ram is a male sheep, the second of the pair

explanation.surface: Two sheep confronting each other in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head to head' means two rams face each other, so the first is turned round; the answer reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse coastal grass planted to bind sand dunes.

clue.text: Prison is more funky!

explanation.surface: A claim that jail is hipper.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a lock-up; also the comparative of a word meaning hip.

clue.text: Aquatic bird has tail bitten off? Goodness me

indicators.note: the bird's last letter is cut away, like a tail nipped off

parts.note: a coot is a water bird

explanation.surface: A water bird loses its tail, prompting surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of mild surprise, like 'well I never'.

clue.text: Musician's son's boast I misconstrued

indicators.note: the words son's boast I are understood wrongly, so their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A player's son brags, and I misread him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musician's' is 'Musician is'; the anagram uses SONS, BOAST and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind player of the low double-reed instrument is a performer.
